title: Kia Launches Syros EV in India From ₹13.49 Lakh With 526 Km Range and 15-Year Battery Warranty
excerpt: Kia's second mass-market EV in India offers two battery options, a Battery-as-a-Service plan starting at ₹7.99 lakh, and an 80% assured buyback after three years.
body:
• Kia Syros EV launched at ₹13.49 lakh (ex-showroom) for the 42 kWh variant, topping out at ₹19.99 lakh for the X-Line Extended Range.
  • The 51.4 kWh battery delivers 526 km ARAI-certified range — the first in its segment to cross the 500 km mark.
  • A Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) option brings ownership cost down to ₹7.99 lakh with battery rental at ₹3.3 per kilometre.
  • Deliveries begin July 30, with a lifetime 15-year battery warranty and up to 80% assured buyback after three years.

Kia India has launched the Syros EV, its second mass-market electric vehicle manufactured in the country, with prices starting at ₹13.49 lakh and deliveries set to begin from July 30 at dealerships across India.

The electric compact SUV arrives amid surging global crude oil prices and India's accelerating push toward clean mobility. It is available in seven variants spread across two battery-pack options: a 42 kWh standard range and a 51.4 kWh extended range.

Range and Performance

The larger 51.4 kWh battery delivers an ARAI-certified MIDC range of 526 km on a single charge — making the Syros EV the first model in its segment to breach the 500 km threshold. The 42 kWh version offers 443 km of certified range.

Both variants draw power from a front-mounted electric motor. The extended-range version produces 169 bhp and 255 Nm of torque, completing the 0-100 km/h sprint in 8.1 seconds. The standard battery variant puts out 133 bhp with the same torque figure.

DC fast charging from 10 to 80 percent takes 39 minutes using a 100 kW charger. The EV also features a 10.8 kW onboard AC charger and battery conditioning that pre-heats or cools the pack before rapid charging sessions.

Pricing and Variants

The seven-variant lineup spans a wide price range:

The 42 kWh variants — HTK (₹13.49 lakh), HTK+ (₹14.99 lakh), and HTX (₹15.99 lakh) — target buyers seeking an affordable entry into electric ownership. Extended Range variants start with the HTK+ ER at ₹16.99 lakh and climb through HTX ER (₹17.99 lakh), HTX+ ER (₹19.49 lakh), to the flagship X-Line ER at ₹19.99 lakh. All prices are ex-showroom.

Ownership and Affordability Push

Kia has bundled aggressive ownership benefits designed to address the anxiety that still keeps many Indian buyers away from EVs. The centrepiece is a Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) financing model that separates battery cost from vehicle cost, bringing the initial ownership price down to ₹7.99 lakh with ongoing battery rental charges from ₹3.3 per kilometre.

"We designed the Syros EV to make electric mobility more accessible without compromising on value."

— Gwanggu Lee, Managing Director and CEO, Kia India

The company is also offering a lifetime high-voltage battery warranty covering 15 years with unlimited kilometres for the first owner, and an assured buyback programme guaranteeing resale value of up to 80 percent after three years.

Features and Platform

Built on Kia's reinforced K1 platform, the Syros EV carries an IP67-rated Nickel Manganese Cobalt battery with liquid-cooled thermal management. Interior highlights include a 30-inch panoramic display cluster comprising a 12.3-inch touchscreen, a 12.3-inch digital instrument panel, and a 5-inch climate control interface. The EV also offers Level 2 ADAS, a dual-pane panoramic sunroof, a 360-degree camera, and a built-in dashcam.

Kia's EV support infrastructure now includes more than 129 dealerships with high-capacity DC fast chargers, 275 EV-ready workshops, and over 900 customer touchpoints across 400 cities.

The Syros EV enters a segment that is becoming fiercely competitive as Tata, Hyundai, and MG all expand their electric lineups. Its 526 km range claim and the BaaS ownership model represent Kia's bet that affordability and range confidence — not just sticker price — will decide the next wave of Indian EV adoption.
